=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:5194-5200 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The retry logic for the 'lite' reviewer tier references an undefined variable `${sf_status}`.
  WHY: The condition `[ "${sf_status}" = "skipped_unmapped" ]` (and subsequent checks for `skipped_open` and `failed`) will evaluate against an empty string, causing the retry condition to always be false. The intended retry logic for Mistral lite reviewers when skipped or encountering context overflows will never execute, potentially allowing the PR to pass with zero successful reviewers in the lite tier.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:5443 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The zero-success guard exempts only `lite` tier reviews and exits 0 when no successful reviewers are found, but only checks `REVIEW_TIER != "lite"`.
  WHY: When `REVIEW_TIER` is explicitly set to `disabled`, the condition `[ "${REVIEW_TIER:-}" != "lite" ]` evaluates to true, potentially bypassing the guard and allowing the review to pass with zero successful reviewers, even when it should have been blocked.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:5443 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new tier guard exempts only the literal value "lite" from the silent exit-0 path.
  WHY: With `REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED=false` and `REVIEWER_RISK_TIER_ENABLED=true`, a sole skipped Mistral reviewer can exit 0 silently with `REVIEWERS_SUCCESSFUL=0`; the Mistral retry also does not fire because it requires `REVIEW_TIER="lite"`. Suggested minimal fix: check the effective reviewer count so any single-reviewer tier fails closed.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:5366-5371 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The contract test asserts the new fail-closed behaviour only for `REVIEW_TIER="lite"` and does not exercise the disabled, trivial, standard, or full tiers.
  WHY: Those paths can regress without the existing test suite detecting it. Suggested minimal fix: parametrise the test over `REVIEW_TIER` in `{"lite", "trivial", "disabled"}` with the same expected fail-closed outcome for single-reviewer slots.
- Requirement: The PR title and description ("AI implementation for issue #6528") and the LINKED ISSUE require (a) withdrawing stale auto-merge on pull_request.synchronize, (b) publishing an `ai-review/head-gate` commit status bound to the evaluated SHA on opened/synchronize and on success, (c) documenting how to require the status in default-branch protection.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, scripts/review_head_gate.sh, scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh, scripts/review_rb_judge.sh, README.md (PR DIFF does touch these).
  Evidence of absence: The PR DIFF does deliver the head-gate implementation, but the LAST RUN DIFF (the most recent autofix iteration this pass is reviewing) modifies a completely unrelated set of files: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh (Mistral lite retry logic), changelog.d/6438-reviewer-panel-random-tiers.md (an issue #6438 changelog entry, not #6528), tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py (Mistral retry tests), README.md and agents.md (Mistral doc updates). The LAST RUN CHANGED FILES contain zero head-gate files. Issue #6528's review feedback — if any was routed through the autofix — therefore appears to have been ignored in favor of edits to a different issue's reviewer-fallback logic in the same PR. This is a scope drift, not an absence of code: the PR delivers #6528, but the LAST RUN did not act on #6528 review signals.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
- changelog.d/6438-reviewer-panel-random-tiers.md: "Mistral was the only lite reviewer" line
  PROBLEM: The doc text ties the new failure mode to "lite" only; it should describe the actual invariant (single-reviewer runs must succeed).
  WHY: The described failure mode is not limited to lite-tier runs.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: If the loop structure changes or the array is empty despite the file-existence check, `sf_status` could be undefined or stale; the reviewer recommends reading the status file directly.

  WHY: A single skipped Mistral reviewer can pass review with no successful reviewer, bypassing the intended safety check.
